name: Text Parser Fallback
description: For the tradition where you type. A verb-noun parser sits alongside the link interface rather than replacing it, so the same story supports both a modern reader and someone who wants to type TAKE LAMP. The parser's honest problem is the unrecognised word, and the response is graded: an unknown verb, a known verb with an unknown noun, and a known pair that is simply not possible here are three different failures and saying which one it was is the difference between a parser that teaches its vocabulary and one that stonewalls. Synonyms are declared, because guessing at them is how a parser becomes a vocabulary quiz.

inputs.name: synonyms
inputs.description: Alternate spellings mapped to canonical verbs.

inputs.name: gradedFailures
inputs.description: Whether unknown-verb, unknown-noun and not-possible-here are reported distinctly.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Whether the parser is offered at all. Off by default: link-based reading is the form most readers expect.

outputs.name: lastCommand
outputs.description: Parsed verb and noun, or the failure kind.

outputs.name: vocabulary
outputs.description: Words the parser will currently accept.
